result.description: All-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project/task management, with AI agents.
result.auth_detail: OAuth 2.0 auth-code for public integrations (any workspace, no review needed to authorize). Internal connection API token and personal access token (PAT) as static Bearer tokens. Each end user can self-create a PAT or internal token. Pages must be shared with the connection.
result.access_detail: Gate audit (1): Public OAuth integration installable in any workspace; docs say authorization can start as soon as client credentials and redirect URI are set, and Marketplace review is optional (listing only). So no vendor review gate. (2): No paid plan needed. Free plan can create internal connections and PATs (Free plan PAT creation is workspace owners only; user's own free workspace makes them owner). Note: PAT policy on Business and Enterprise is admin-controlled, but OAuth is unaffected.
result.api_notes: REST at api.notion.com, versioned via the Notion-Version header (2026-03-11). Covers pages, databases, blocks, comments, users, search, file uploads, and an Admin API for enterprise. Official JS SDK. Page-level access requires explicit sharing with the connection.

evidence.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review is not required.
A PAT acts as the user who created it and uses that user's permissions in the selected workspace.
This makes the integration eligible for Marketplace listing, subject to review. Listing is optional.
A public integration is an OAuth integration that users can install in any Notion workspace.
| Free | Workspace owners only. | Not configurable. |
